_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::structural_mechanics#14 — KINEM linear on an ordinary St-Venant-Kirchhoff solid never errors: it drops the geometric nonlinearity, over-predicts compliance and the run looks perfectly healthy, so the only defence is a converged comparison. Four arms of one HEX8 unit cube (YOUNG 1000, NUE 0.3, surface Neumann in y), two load levels a factor 300 apart, run 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C. Each linear arm carries its NONLINEAR twin's RESULT DESCRIPTION pinned at 1e-12 at TWO probe nodes at once, node 6 and node 3, because the size of the discrepancy is node-dependent and a percentage quoted without a node means nothing. Observed: at the small load the two kinematics agree to 0.06% and the SIGN differs between the probe nodes (-0.06% at node 6, +0.06% at node 3), so the direction of the error is no tell at small strain; at 300x the load KINEM linear over-predicts by +5.70% at node 6 and +81.84% at the SAME run's node 3. Both nonlinear references exit 0 with no result failures, both linear runs are stopped only by the result test this fixture adds (SMALL/BIG_ONLY_ERROR_IS_THE_RESULT_TEST=yes) and neither log ever prints the word KINEM (*_MENTIONS_KINEM=0) — in a deck without a result test there is nothing at all to grep for.

_mutation.note: remove the pathology from the large-load arm: give it the nonlinear kinematics. It then matches its twin at both probe nodes, both percentages become 'agrees' and EXIT_LIN_BIG becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
remove the pathology from the small-load arm too. The 0.06% pair disappears and EXIT_LIN_SMALL becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
